stories.headline: Delhi Police detain at least 100 with criminal records in overnight ops. ahead of CJP protest
stories.deck: Those detained from across 15 districts were suspected of joining the CJP-led protest at Jantar Mantar, sources said
stories.bodyText:
Delhi Police have detained at least 100 people with criminal records in overnight operations across 15 districts, sources told The Hindu. They were allegedly suspected of joining Saturday’s (October 10, 2026) planned protest by the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) at Jantar Mantar amid the ongoing Election Commission row.
Also Read : Delhi protest against CEC LIVE
At least 100 people with criminal records have been detained across 15 districts of the national capital as part of a preventive measure, the source added.
Earlier, the Delhi Police denied permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing alleged non-compliance with conditions agreed upon during an earlier demonstration. Joint Commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Nupur Prasad said on Friday (October 9, 2026) that the permission was sought in the last minute while as per rules it should be sort atleast 10 days before the protest.
The CJP had maintained that it was informing the police rather than seeking permission, arguing that Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site and that the police should facilitate a peaceful gathering. Mr. Das had submitted the letter at Parliament Street police station and received an acknowledgement, according to the organisers.
As Delhi prepares for the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, traffic diversions will be enforced from 6 a.m. on Saturday (October 10, 2026), affecting movement at 30 key points across Delhi, police said.
Authorities have also taken several other measures ahead of the protest, including internet curbs in parts of Delhi, the shutting down of markets and Metro stations, and the cancelling dozens of trains bound for the capital.
With PTI inputs

stories.headline: The versatility of Nana Patekar
stories.bodyText: Some actors can tell you everything about a character without spelling it out in dialogue. You understand who they are through their silences, mannerisms and the smallest shifts in expression. Nana Patekar had a way of making even a brief appearance memorable. Much of it was in the details — the way he spoke, paused, looked and reacted. It is that lived-in quality that makes his characters so striking, irrespective of how big or small they were. . In Mira Nair’s ‘Salaam Bombay!’ (1988), for example, he plays the pimp, Baba. The menacing nature of the pimp comes through in his way of speaking, his physical presence and the way he treats the children and women around him as commodities, leaving a strong impact on the audience within a brief screen time. He never once makes grand declarations about how dangerous he is. . He uses a similar method in the 1989 crime drama ‘Parinda’, directed by Vidhu Vinod Chopra. The crazy, ruthless and erratic underworld don Anna Seth is one of the most memorable villains of Indian cinema. Nana brought a quiet, unpredictable, and unsettling intensity to the character that was psychotic as well as vulnerable — the distinct asthmatic wheeze made Anna Seth grounded and uncomfortably realistic. The film also won him a national award. .Nana Patekar: When the actor’s presence became performance. It is his ability to inhabit a character that makes Uday Shetty so iconic that he continues to remain an enduring part of pop culture and internet memes. In the slapstick comedy ‘Welcome’, Nana portrays a fierce, hot-headed don who is also very emotional when it comes to his sister. He brought the same intensity of his other characters to play the campy villain and understood that deadpan silence or a slow, dangerous glare was often funnier than a punchline. His internal dialogues, the most famous one being ‘Control, Uday, control’, have become a defining part of the film’s popularity. . Three ‘villains’, similar approaches but three different characteristics — that defines Nana’s versatility. . In his most commercially successful film ‘Krantiveer’ (1994), his Pratap is all fury — volatile, abrasive and theatrical, but never detached from the character’s political conviction. The film was released in the aftermath of the 1993 Bombay riots; in one of its most remembered scenes, Pratap slits his palm, and then slits the palms of a Hindu and a Muslim fighting with and blaming one another for the communal riots. He points to the blood flowing from their palms that has now mixed and asks, ‘Yeh Musalman ka khoon, yeh Hindu ka khoon… bata, ismein Musalman ka kaunsa, Hindu ka kaunsa, bata’. Three decades later, the question still remains relevant. . Nana plays the poignant Vasant in Sai Paranjpye’s ‘Disha’, which explores the harsh realities of rural poverty and urban labour migration. Although Vasant believes true life is in the village, he has to continue working in Bombay’s cotton mills for survival. But unlike his character, Nana returned to his village, often describing how he finds comfort in simple living surrounded by mountains. He also set up the NAAM Foundation to support farmers and rural communities in drought-prone areas like Marathwada and Vidarbha, aiding families in distress. . After his sudden death on Thursday morning, what now remains is an actor whose characters could stay with the audience long after the scenes were over — whether he was playing a ruthless hustler, a hot-headed gangster, a theatre legend, a philosophical strategist or a migrant worker.

stories.headline: ‘Obvious weakness’: Zelenskyy slams Trump’s Russian diesel deal
stories.bodyText:
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday (local time) warned that easing sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement would be an “obvious weakness” that could prolong the war by allowing Moscow to continue selling petroleum products.
In a post on X, Zelenskyy said peace could not be achieved through weakness and called for stronger sanctions, continued support for Ukraine and sustained pressure on Moscow to end the war.
"Peace never comes through weakness. Today, representatives of the US Congress were in Kyiv – a bipartisan delegation – and I am grateful to them for visiting Ukraine at such a difficult time. They asked: what is needed to end the war? The answer must be strong. There must be sanctions under the Lindsey Graham bill, there must be support for Ukraine in protecting lives, and there must be pressure on Russia for its war. And today, there was a conversation between the leaders of America and Russia. A conversation that leads to something different," he wrote.
Referring to the diesel announcement, Zelenskyy said, “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world. 
Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged."
"Recently, there was a European decision to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs. Since then, Russian strikes and the torment of people have only increased," he added.
Citing recent Russian attacks across Ukraine, Zelenskyy said, "This past week alone, there was a brutal Russian missile strike on a residential building in Pryluky, aerial bombs were dropped on Kramatorsk – on ordinary city buses – and there have been constant attacks on Kyiv’s energy infrastructure and on the life-sustaining infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa, and our other cities. Dozens of people have been killed and hundreds wounded."
He alleged that Russia was resorting to such attacks because it was struggling to achieve its objectives on the battlefield. "The Russians are compensating for their inability to achieve their objectives on the battlefield with this kind of terror. This year, Russia is weaker on the battlefield than at any other point in the war. That is why Putin is relying on terror. That is why he is relying on attempts to strike backroom deals to secure some form of pressure relief for Russia, in order to buy more time and more opportunities for war," he further said.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine was prepared to take reciprocal steps towards de-escalation, adding that the American team was aware of Kyiv’s position.
"Ukraine is ready to take symmetrical de-escalatory steps, and the American team knows our position. Our strikes on Russian oil refineries and other oil facilities are a response to Russia’s years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine’s energy sector. Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure. This is the kind of agreement we are proposing to America, and we believe the United States has enough power to achieve such a compromise," he said.

Zelenskyy’s remarks came after US President Donald Trump spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin and announced a deal to secure diesel supplies from Russia, marking a shift in Washington’s pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine as the US seeks to address rising fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.
In a social media post on Friday, Trump said Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”. He added that Russia would deliver another 3 million tonnes “within a short period of time”.
The announcement came just a month after Trump signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law aimed at curbing Moscow’s oil and gas revenues, which help fund its war against Ukraine.

stories.headline: Trump says Norway has 'indelible stain' for not awarding him Nobel Peace Prize
stories.deck: The U.S. President called Navi Pillay a “mystery ​person” during a ‌campaign rally in Syracuse, New York. “I never heard of the person. Nobody did.”
stories.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump reiterated his complaints on Friday (October 9, 2026) about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, calling it a disgraceful and embarrassing decision that had left a stain on Norway, which hosts the Nobel committee.
Mr. Trump unleashed on Norway hours after the committee awarded this year’s prize to Navi Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge who oversaw a UN report that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Mr. Trump called Ms. Pillay a “mystery person” during a campaign rally in Syracuse, New York. “I never heard of the person. Nobody did.”
Each year of his presidency, Mr. Trump has expressed disappointment at his failure to win the prize.
“This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Mr. Trump said.
He listed a number of conflicts that he claimed a role in resolving and said he has helped prevent wars from breaking out between North and South Korea, Japan and North Korea, and China and Taiwan, without providing evidence.
“The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization. And we will not forget, Norway,” he said.

stories.headline: Song stories | The timeless mysticism of ‘Sanson Ki Mala’
stories.bodyText: At London’s Wembley Stadium last month, during Diljit Dosanjh’s Aura World Tour, the entire stadium erupted in a frenzied uproar at the familiar notes of ‘Sanson ki maala pe simroon main pi ka naam…’ Amidst the stadium-rock arrangement of soaring, metal-esque guitar and punchy arena drums, Diljit appeared like a Sufi lost in a spiritual trance. . Famously attributed to the 16th-century mystic poet Mira Bai, the verse expresses supreme surrender and divine love. Translating to ‘On the rosary of my breath, I chant my beloved’s name’, it represents yearning through every single breath. The beloved (pi) symbolises Krishna, whom Mira Bai deeply adored. . ‘Sanson Ki Mala’ was immortalised as a Sufi-qawwali by the legendary Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, with the verses written by Punjabi-Urdu poet Tufail Hoshiarpuri. Bittersweet pangs of separation and ecstatic longing are conveyed through paradoxical imagery such as ‘angaron par neend aa jaye, kaanton par aaram’ (finding comfort on burning coal and a bed of thorns) — illustrating the heart so consumed by the divine taste of love that it numbs physical suffering. .Bengaluru rapper blends nadaswaram with West Coast hip-hop. Apart from Nusrat’s signature sargams and taans, ‘Sanson Ki Mala’ has an exceptionally sturdy melodic spine, which music analysts believe makes the song instantly recognisable even when adapted into modern genres: a beautiful reflection of Nusrat’s genius, perhaps at the same time exposing the limitations of anyone trying to dress it up. And that is why the many renditions, the one in ‘Koyla’ and a recent one in ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’, sound weak and performative. Diljit’s rendition perhaps worked because it picked genuine soulful surrender over empty commercial arrangement. . Nusrat also transformed the bhajan into a cross-cultural bridge between Bhakti poetry and Sufi spiritualism — he added the lines ‘ek tha saajan mandir mein, aur ek tha pritam masjid mein, par’, before ‘prem ki rang mein aisi doobi, ban gaya ek hi roop’, translating to ‘One lover was in the temple and the other in the mosque, but I was so deeply immersed in the colour of love that both became one single form’. Today, the song acts as a deeply secular bridge, dissolving religious and geographical boundaries. . Song Stories is a monthly column that takes up an iconic number and explores why it still lives rent-free in our heads.

Jaishankar highlights shared aspirations, self-reliance in India-Africa partnership
briefs.deck: S. Jaishankar arrived in Ethiopia on October 8 from Côte d’Ivoire on the final leg of his three-nation tour of African countries, which also included Ghana.
briefs.bodyText:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Friday (October 9, 2026) highlighted the historic India-Africa partnership, rooted in shared solidarity and a common pursuit of fairness, representation, and the freedom to shape their own future, while outlining key areas of cooperation between the two sides.
Mr. Jaishankar arrived in Ethiopia on Thursday (October 8, 2026) from Côte d’Ivoire on the final leg of his three-nation tour of African countries, which also included Ghana.
Addressing a gathering at the Adwa Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa, Mr. Jaishankar said the development visions of India and Africa emphasised industrialisation, which should not be denied by flooding markets with cheap goods or restricting market access.
He highlighted the robust trade and investment ties between India and African countries across sectors such as manufacturing, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, energy, mining, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services and information technology.
Mr. Jaishankar said self-reliance was a shared conviction that provided a strong foundation for the enduring partnership between India and Africa.
India's development partnership with African countries was guided by the priorities of partner nations, he said, adding that India has "supported more than 220 projects" in areas such as "power generation, electricity transmission, water, agriculture, railways, healthcare, manufacturing and public infrastructure".
He also highlighted India's capacity-building initiatives, saying more than 70,000 African students and professionals had received support from India over the past decade.
Emphasising the growing role of technology in bilateral cooperation, Jaishankar pointed to the transformative impact of digital governance and expanding cooperation on India Stack.
"The transformative impact of digital governance, as well as growing India Stack cooperation with Africa. Space, drones, and AI are new frontiers of this cooperation," he said.
Mr. Jaishankar also underlined India's efforts to strengthen Africa's health security through vaccine support, pharmaceutical investments and the gifting of Bhabhatron cancer treatment machines.
In a separate post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said India and Ethiopia shared the vision of 'AI for All' and its potential to advance development and prosperity.
He also visited the Ethiopia Science Museum, describing it as a symbol of the country's efforts to build a technology-driven, knowledge-based economy. Science and innovation cooperation would play a greater role in the India-Ethiopia strategic partnership, he said.

briefs.headline: 9/11 attacks inspired flydubai hijacker to become a pilot: UAE probe
briefs.bodyText:
The co-pilot and alleged hijacker of a flydubai flight and crash it into Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport was inspired by the September 11, 2001, terror attacks in the US, according to preliminary findings released by the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Hamam al-Hammami, 29, who was serving as the co-pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30, allegedly planned to take control of the aircraft and crash it into the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport, Israel’s main international airport.
According to a statement by UAE attorney general Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, shared by Emirati state media, al-Hammami wanted to carry out an attack similar to the 9/11 attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people in the US 25 years ago. Four commercial planes were hijacked during those attacks and crashed at three locations.
“The idea of carrying out a similar operation using an aircraft became firmly established in his mind, which, according to his confessions, was connected to his decision to pursue a career in aviation,” Friday’s statement said.
The co-pilot allegedly planned “a premeditated plot with a terrorist objective, aimed at taking control of the aircraft and using it to carry out a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport,” with the aim of causing “the greatest possible number of casualties,” the statement added.
Flew to Israel twice before alleged attack
The preliminary investigation found that the September 30 flight was not al-Hammami’s first trip to Ben Gurion Airport. He had reportedly taken part in two earlier flights to the airport to familiarise himself with the route and the airport before carrying out the alleged attack.
An Israeli official and another source familiar with the matter had earlier told CNN that the suspected hijacker likely intended to target the airport, Israel’s main international gateway.
The alleged hijacking attempt was stopped after the captain and several passengers restrained al-Hammami and regained control of the aircraft.
How the co-pilot became radicalised
The UAE investigation found that al-Hammami began moving towards extremism and terrorism in 2017, while studying in Australia. He was reportedly influenced by extremist publications and online content that praised terrorist groups and suicide attacks.
According to the statement, he “prepared himself psychologically and physically to carry out his plot by increasing his exposure to material inciting terrorism and training in boxing under a private coach.”
Investigators also examined his employment history with different airlines.
Al-Hammami worked for Oman Air from 2020 to 2024. He joined Royal Air Maroc in 2025 but worked there for only a few months before moving to Flydubai in January 2026, according to the UAE statement.
A source had earlier told CNN that Oman Air removed al-Hammami from flight training because of concerns about his radical views and assigned him another role at the airline.
In a statement to the Associated Press last week, Royal Air Maroc said al-Hammami had undergone three months of training with the airline in 2025 as part of its pre-employment process but was not selected for a job.
Flydubai recruitment procedures under scrutiny
The UAE investigation also examined how Flydubai hired al-Hammami. Investigators found that he had met the professional and security requirements for the job, including holding a pilot’s licence, possessing a certificate of good conduct and passing the required examinations.
“There were “no indications emerging during those procedures that revealed his extremist inclinations or his intention to carry out a terrorist plot,” attorney general Al Shamsi said, according to Emirati state media.
Al-Hammami told investigators that he had acted alone, but authorities are still checking his claim.

briefs.headline: Ishnidh Virdi, Keya Kumar Badugu win golf titles
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Local lad Ishnidh Singh Virdi completed a splendid wire-to-wire victory at the IGU Rotary Southern India Bio-Gen Sansera Amateur Golf Championships at the KGA course on Friday. . Virdi shot a closing three-under-par 69 for an impressive four-day total of 10-under 278. Ranveer Mitroo (71) and Harjai Milkha Singh (76) -- who suffered a meltdown on the final day -- finished tied at two-under 286. Prince Bainsla (72) finished fourth at one-under 287, making him the only other amateur to break par. . Virdi got off to a sedate start even as his challengers fell behind early in the round. The 17-year-old got going with a 15-foot birdie putt on the eighth hole. He followed that up with further birdies on the 10th, 11th and 15th holes to leave the rest to battle for the second spot. His lone blemish came on the 17th hole. .Asian Games 2026 | ‘If Rory and Nelly could do it, so can I’: How Pranavi Urs invoked the spirit of golf greats to win historic gold. In the Ladies and Junior Girls’ event, Keya Kumar Badugu rallied in brilliant fashion on the homestretch to edge out Anaahat Bindra -- who did all the front-running -- on the first playoff hole. The two were tied at one-under 215 after 54 holes. . Keya, who began the day one stroke off the lead, slipped four behind after the 10th hole. However, the Delhi youngster, playing in only her second tournament of the season, didn’t let it bog her down. The 19-year-old fired a hat-trick of birdies from the 15th to catch up with the leader. . In the playoff, Keya came up with a brilliant drive and then chipped to three feet for another birdie to walk away with the title and the winner’s purse of Rs 75,000. . briefs.headline: Birth centenary | The days of Raaj Kumar
briefs.deck: Birth centenary | The days of Raaj
briefs.bodyText: Bollywood stars can be enigmatic, eccentric, or controversial, but rarely all. Then there’s Raaj Kumar. He paired his famous catchphrase ‘Jaani’ with a smirk, swagger, and spotless shoes and built a larger-than-life persona that’s both charismatic and caricaturish. That raspy drawl delivered scathing insults and sultry lines with equal ease. Even now, his devil-may-care dialogues feature in memes. Zingers from old interviews such as “I don’t admire myself, I respect myself” are the stuff of aura edits, proving he was a dialogue legend in real life, too. . Born Kulbhushan Pandit in rugged Balochistan to a Kashmiri family, Raaj Kumar came from an era of actors whose cinematic sensibilities were influenced by their pre-partition roots. A well-read and articulate polyglot, he was fluent in Urdu, Hindi, and English. An army man’s son, he studied in several Pakistani cities before moving to India. He put his linguistic proficiency and eloquence to remarkable use when he left his police job to pursue a career in showbiz. . And what a career it was. From breaking out with auteur Mehboob Khan’s classic ‘Mother India’ (1957) to becoming the leading man for the passion projects of two other auteurs — Chetan Anand’s ‘Heer Raanjha’ (1970) and Kamal Amrohi’s ‘Pakeezah’ (1972), Raaj Kumar worked with filmmakers of every hue: Ram Maheshwari, Eshmayeel Shroff, Mehul Kumar and more. He wasn’t always the guy who got the girl. Although not considered conventionally attractive, his brooding eyes and chiselled jawline had admirers. He hardly danced or did comedy. Often he wasn’t central to a story; his characters were morally complex, but he was the scene stealer. Kumar’s stardom is best summed up by Kumkum singing to him in ‘Ujala’ (1959): ‘Tera jalwa jisne dekha woh tera ho gaya’. .The ‘Mahanayak’ who questioned his own stardom: Uttam Kumar’s other legacy. Between the natural, non-showy performances of ‘Dil Apna Aur Preet Parai’ (1960), ‘Dil Ek Mandir’ (’63), ‘Oonche Log’ (’65), and ‘Neel Kamal’ (’68), playing the heel in ‘Ujala’, and the challenging characters of ‘Kaajal’ (1965) and ‘Lal Patthar’ (’71), came his turning point: Yash Chopra’s ‘Waqt’ (1965). As the debonair thief Raja courting danger, he got the best of Akhtar Ul Iman’s sharp dialogues and owned them with his cool, controlled, almost lyrical delivery and style. There’s flair in his songs too: the breeziness in ‘Neele Gagan’ (‘Hamraaz’, 1967), the undercurrent in his wordless exchange with Meena Kumari in ‘Ajeeb Dastaan’ (‘Dil Apna…’), or how tenderly he enacts Rafi’s whispering voice in ‘Meri Duniya’ before pivoting to dramatic despair in ‘Yeh Duniya’ (‘Heer Raanjha’). Anand’s retelling of the Punjabi folk epic unfolds entirely in verse, and Raaj Kumar’s innate understanding of poetry, rhythm, and expression made him the natural choice for Raanjha. . Similarly, he plays Salim — the fair-minded nobleman who falls for a courtesan in ‘Pakeezah’ — with the right touch of elegance, intensity and theatricality. His iconic ‘Aapke paaon dekhe’ note admiring Sahibjaan’s (Meena Kumari) pretty feet in that velvety voice, delivered with flawless intonation, crisp enunciation, and old-world courtesy, is unforgettable. But the magic begins in the preceding scene. Salim accidentally enters the sleeping Sahibjaan’s train compartment and catches a glimpse of her feet. Swaying in a moving train, its rhythm is no different from that of the heartbeat of the man who has hopelessly fallen in love. His instant wonder and the demeanour of complete surrender with a dramatic sigh at the sight of the anklet-adorned, alta-dipped feet have a dreaminess that’s lost to time. . Contrast this with the much-overlooked performance in Trilok Jetley’s ‘Godaan’ (1964), where Raaj Kumar brings Hori Mahato, the tragic protagonist of Premchand’s literary classic, to life. As a poor peasant in an oppressive, feudal society who dreams of owning a cow, the actor portrays Hori’s dignified hope, endurance, and eventual resignation with admirable honesty. . Raaj Kumar’s massy image dominated his 1980s filmography. Following the charismatic professor from ‘Bulundi’ (1981) and the swaggering don of ‘Marte Dam Tak’ (1987) was the peak bombast of Brigadier Suryadev (‘Tirangaa’, 1993). The velvet co-ords wearing, cigar-smoking, master of insults is a pop-culture milestone who made fuse conductors fun. But by now, his films had degraded; he was performing on autopilot. . Raaj Kumar’s career was full of memorable associations with formidable co-stars. His chemistry with Meena Kumari did wonders. With Mala Sinha, he attempted diverse genres like ‘Mere Huzoor’ (1968) and ‘36 Ghante’ (’74). Teaming up with a fiery Nana Patekar in ‘Tirangaa’, balancing Danny Denzongpa in a double role in ‘Bulundi’, and sparring verses with Naseeruddin Shah in ‘Police Public’ (1990) gave fans plenty to relish. The ultimate clash was Subhash Ghai’s ‘Saudagar’ (1991), where his screen rivalry with Dilip Kumar circled back to their long-standing real-life feud from the ‘Paigham’ (1959) days in which they played brothers with differing ideologies. Like the line in their famous duet ‘Imli Ka Boota’ goes, ‘Iss jungle mein hum do sher’, the Tragedy King was perhaps the only contemporary Raaj Kumar considered his match. . The old press is filled with juicy gossip about Raaj Kumar’s unpredictability, how his wigs and supposed receding hairline were taboo topics, and his infamous run-ins with peers. He’s described as a man of fascinating contradictions: smug, eccentric, but thoroughly self-aware. Friends and colleagues speak of an intelligent, private individual who didn’t suffer fools. However, darker episodes like an early-career trial and acquittal in a fatal case, or his tirades against journalists questioning leniency in son Puru’s 1990s hit-and-run case, reveal a deeply problematic side that can’t be brushed off. Even today, he remains a polarising figure in the industry, whose personality inspires apocryphal anecdotes like no other matinee star. . The author is a freelance journalist who writes about vintage Hindi cinema.

briefs.headline: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida as Category 2 storm
briefs.deck: Hurricane Isaias has made its presence felt near Destin, Florida, registering maximum sustained winds of 105 mph. Residents in coastal areas across Florida's Panhandle and Alabama are on high alert. In response, officials issued hurricane warnings, with some counties mandating evacuations. To bolster emergency measures, Florida's National Guard mobilized 5,000 personnel, assisting in rescue…
briefs.bodyText:
Hurricane Isaias has made landfall near Destin, Florida, with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 kph), according to the US National Hurricane Center (NHC), Reuters reported on Friday. The storm is located about 50 miles (80 km) west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, the agency said in its latest advisory.
The landfall comes as coastal communities across Florida's Panhandle and parts of Alabama prepare for damaging winds, flooding and a potentially life-threatening storm surge. Earlier forecasts warned that water levels could rise by 6 to 9 feet in vulnerable coastal areas.
“Things are going to get really, really treacherous over the next couple hours,” Jamie Rhome, deputy director of the National Hurricane Center, said earlier, according to the Associated Press (AP).
Authorities have issued hurricane warnings from Ocean Springs in Mississippi to the western Florida Panhandle, while several counties have ordered mandatory evacuations. Mobile, Alabama, has also imposed a curfew as officials prepare for the storm's impact.
More than 365,000 customers in Florida and Alabama were without electricity on Friday evening, according to poweroutage.com. Officials in Mobile reported fallen trees and power lines, while the Emerald Coast Utilities Authority issued a boil-water notice for some customers in Florida.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis warned residents to prepare for power outages, fuel shortages and the possible closure of bridges and highways. The state's National Guard deployed around 5,000 soldiers and airmen to support emergency operations, while search-and-rescue teams were placed on standby. Some prisons also evacuated inmates.
Residents have been securing their homes and filling sandbags to limit potential flood damage. In Panama City, people braved heavy rain to protect their properties ahead of the storm.
Anne Petzold, a resident of Gulf Breeze, said she and her husband had installed hurricane shutters and cleared their yard of objects that could become dangerous in high winds.
“Everybody does what they can do, everybody asks if they need help — they ask for help, they offer help. All good,” she said. “It's just another adventure.”
The NHC has forecast 4 to 8 inches of rainfall, with localised totals potentially reaching 15 inches in parts of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southwestern Georgia. The storm is expected to weaken as it moves inland, but flooding and hazardous weather could continue across parts of the southeastern US.

briefs.headline: Delhi braces for CJP protest: 45 metro stations shut, trains cancelled, 23,000 security personnel deployed
briefs.deck: Here is everything you need to know about the massive security lockdown in Delhi ahead of the CJP’s October 10 protest.
briefs.bodyText:
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), along with student organisations, social activists and farmer groups, gears up for a massive protest on Saturday (October 10, 2026), authorities have tightened security and imposed traffic restrictions across New Delhi.
The CJP, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, along with other student bodies such as All India Students Association (AISA) and AISF, announced a nationwide march to Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the complete rollback of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Protestors allege that the SIR exercise is being misused to tamper with voter lists by deleting genuine voters, misclassifying living citizens as deceased despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive and altering key registration documents like Form 6 without consent.
45 metro stations closed
The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has announced the closure of 45 metro stations on Saturday in view of the prevailing law and order situation. The move follows DMRC’s earlier order of closure of 57 metro stations, which got revoked after Supreme Court directed Central Government to lift stringent restrictions.
On Friday night, the DMRC posted in X, “Due to security reasons, the entry and exit at the following metro stations will remain closed from 09:00 PM on 9th October, 2026 till 06:00 PM on 10th October, 2026. Further the situation will be reviewed by the security agencies and necessary updates will be shared accordingly. However, interchange facility will remain available at all the concerned metro stations except New Delhi metro station”.
Major transit hubs such as Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Kashmere Gate, Hauz Khas, and Supreme Court are among the closed locations.
Trains cancelled and diverted
Similarly, railway zones across the country, including Western Railway, Central Railway, Northern Railway and North-Western Railway, have cancelled or rescheduled over 200 trains coming into or originating from Delhi citing severe road traffic congestion around New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.
Western Railway rescheduled the Mumbai Central–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (12951) and August Kranti Rajdhani Express (12953) by five hours, while cancelling services like the Bandra Terminus–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (12247), Dr. Ambedkar Nagar–New Delhi Express (20155), Indore–Hazrat Nizamuddin Express (09309), Indore–New Delhi Express (12415), and Sabarmati–New Delhi Express (12957). Central Railway cancelled the CSMT–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express (22221) and CSMT–New Delhi Rajdhani Express (22209. The North Western Railway on Friday (October 9) cancelled 13 train services scheduled to depart for the national capital on October 9 and 10, citing “operational reasons”. Meanwhile, the Jammu railway division on Friday announced the cancellation of four key trains heading to the national capital, including the superfast Rajdhani Express.
This includes 75 Mail/Express including Rajdhani, Tejas, Shatabdi, and 170 passenger trains.
Railways has set up dedicated helpdesks and officials clarified that passengers with valid, verified train tickets will be allowed access to stations.
23,000 security personnel deployed
The Ministry of Home Affairs has provided the Delhi Police with additional companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) to strengthen security arrangements in view of the proposed protest and other potential gatherings in the national capital.
According to sources, around 23,000 security personnel are expected to be deployed across Delhi between October 8, 2026 and October 12, 2026.
The New Delhi area is expected to witness extensive security deployment on October 10, 2026, with multi-layered barricading, CCTV surveillance and Facial Recognition System (FRS)-enabled cameras being used to monitor movement.
Strict vigil will be maintained at Delhi’s borders, railway stations and bus terminals. Security agencies are also keeping a special watch to prevent criminal elements from entering protest gatherings by posing as protesters, sources said.
Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force, and gatherings in violation of the restrictions will not be permitted.
Depending on the situation, police may also regulate access to metro stations and markets in the New Delhi area.
Security agencies are maintaining close coordination and monitoring developments ahead of October 10 to prevent any law-and-order situation in the national capital, sources said.
Other closures: schools, colleges, liquor shops shut
The Delhi government ordered all retail liquor vendors to remain closed on October 9, 2026 and October 10, 2026, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. Multiple educational institutions including Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, shifted classes online and postponed scheduled events
Who are joining the CJP protest
Despite the Delhi Police denying permission for the protests, citing past rule violations and short application notice, several civil groups and prominent leaders have shown their interest in participating in the protests.
Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has announced that his family and he will join the protest at Jantar Mantar. AISA national president and student activist Neha Bora urged participants across the country to hold local sit-ins wherever they are. The demonstration will continue along with the Left student groups, farmers associations and civil rights groups.
CJP leaders including Mr. Dipke, Sayrav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will be leading the agitation.

stories.headline: Audit of more than 120 public parks in Bengaluru finds accessibility gaps
stories.deck: When it comes to sanitation, only 29.5% have toilets, of which 61% are accessible. Only 5.4% have handwashing facilities, and 10.9% have drinking water
stories.bodyText:
An audit of more than 120 public parks across Bengaluru has found gaps in accessibility across entrances, pathways, facilities, signage and play areas.
Only 34.8% of the surveyed parks allow wheelchair users to enter without encountering a barrier.
The survey was conducted by Pacta, a Bengaluru-based law firm and policy think tank, which launched Bengaluru Parks Observatory, an interactive dashboard which includes the survey findings.
According to the organisation, it is India’s first citizen-audited accessibility dashboard for public parks.
Findings
Between June and July, volunteers physically visited the parks and assessed each against a common accessibility checklist created by Pacta. The checklist covers entrances, pathways, signage, play areas, maintenance, facilities and operations. Every submission was geotagged and mapped to its municipal corporation.
Among the surveyed parks, only 36.2% have a ramp at the entrance, and 46.4% have a step-free main entrance. Around 62% have pathways smooth enough for independent wheelchair use, and 71% are free of obstructions such as parked vehicles, vendors or debris.
When it comes to sanitation, only 29.5% have toilets, of which 61% are accessible. Only 5.4% have handwashing facilities, and 10.9% have drinking water. While 81.9% have entrance signage, only 10.6% have a park map. Around 73% have play equipment, and 75.5% of that equipment can be used at least partly across ability levels.
Live dashboard
“Accessibility is really about whether anyone can step out of their home and use the shared spaces of their city with ease and dignity. This audit gives Bengaluru an honest starting point. There is a good foundation in many parks, and there are clear gaps that can be closed with the right attention and resources. We see this data as a common map rather than a verdict, and our hope is that the city, funders and residents will use it together,” said Nivedita Krishna, founder, Pacta.
The team members noted that the observatory, available at parks.pacta.in/dashboard, will remain a continuously updated record of accessibility across Bengaluru’s public parks with the help of citizens and volunteers.

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s gig season is serving major FOMO
stories.deck: From Guns N’ Roses and Diljit to Fred again.., Shreya Ghoshal and Raghu Dixit, here’s your three-month guide to the city’s biggest nights — and the gigs worth saving up for
stories.bodyText:
Your weekends are booked. Your Spotify playlists are about to become real-life experiences. And your bank account? Well, that may need a pep talk. Bengaluru’s concert calendar is looking seriously stacked for the next three months, with rock royalty, Bollywood favourites, Punjabi pop, indie sounds, electronic heavyweights and full-blown music festivals taking over the city.
There’s something for almost every mood — whether you want to scream along to a rock classic, dance until your feet give up, rediscover a Bollywood favourite or spend an entire weekend inside a music festival.
There’s just one problem: some weekends are going to make you choose. So charge your phone, check your calendar, assemble your concert crew — and maybe start saving now. Because Bengaluru's biggest concert-season problem isn't going to be finding something to do. It's going to be figuring out which FOMO you can afford.
OCTOBER - The warm-up before things get wild
October eases Bengaluru into concert season with a little bit of everything — Bollywood celebrity, metal mayhem, indie-folk energy and an immersive musical experience.
OCT 10 | HARD ROCK & HEAVY METAL FESTIVAL
BITS Club Grounds | 1 pm
Not into Bollywood? Turn the volume all the way up. The Hard Rock and Heavy Metal Festival is for the crowd that considers distortion, screaming guitars and headbanging a perfectly good way to spend a Saturday.
October 10 dilemma: Bollywood star or metal mayhem? Choose your fighter.
OCT 24 | THE RAGHU DIXIT PROJECT
Orion Mall | 6.30 pm
Few artistes sound as Bengaluru as Raghu Dixit. His folk-meets-rock sound, infectious energy and unmistakable stage presence make this one a natural pick for the city’s indie and live-music crowd.
Your vibe:
 Bengaluru pride, folk-rock and singing along with the entire room.
OCT 24 | SONU NIGAM – THE REVOLUTION INDIA TOUR
Bhartiya Mall of Bengaluru | 7 pm
On the other side of the city, Sonu Nigam is bringing a catalogue packed with Bollywood nostalgia. If your playlist jumps effortlessly from ’90s classics to current Hindi hits, this one should hit the sweet spot.
October 24 problem:
 Raghu Dixit or Sonu Nigam? Indie energy or Bollywood feels?
OCT 31 | DAMROOH BY RICKY KEJ
District Arena @ Terraform | 6 pm
Halloween gets a musical twist as Grammy-winning composer Ricky Kej brings Damrooh to Bengaluru. Expect something beyond a conventional concert, with music, technology and an immersive experience coming together.
Your vibe:
 music, visuals and something a little different.
NOVEMBER - Okay, now Bengaluru is showing off
November takes the concert calendar from “busy” to how are we supposed to attend all of these? Rock legends, Punjabi stars, playback royalty and contemporary pop acts arrive — with multiple major gigs landing on the same weekends.
NOV 14 | GUNS N’ ROSES INDIA TOUR
NICE Grounds | 4 pm
The rock gods are coming. Guns N’ Roses bring their India tour to Bengaluru, promising giant riffs, stadium-sized energy and the kind of set where the crowd probably knows the words before Axl Rose even starts singing.
Your vibe:
 rock T-shirts, air guitars and losing your voice.
NOV 14 | PAPON LIVE
District Arena @ Terraform | 7 pm
Prefer something more eclectic? Papon brings his blend of folk, contemporary sounds, Bollywood and Indian musical influences to the city.
The clash:
 Guns N’ Roses vs Papon. Two very different Saturday nights. One calendar.
NOV 20 | SATINDER SARTAaj LIVE
District Arena | 7 pm
For those who like their music with poetry and plenty of feels, Satinder Sartaaj brings his distinctive Punjabi sound to Bengaluru.
Your vibe:
 lyrical, soulful and slightly dreamy.
NOV 21 | MADHUBANTI BAGCHI – THIS IS WHO WE ARE INDIA TOUR
Phoenix Marketcity, 
Whitefield | 7
 pm
Madhubanti Bagchi brings her contemporary sound to Bengaluru with This Is Who We Are. Expect a more intimate, current-pop mood — a nice change of pace from November’s giant arena shows.
NOV 22 | SHREYA GHOSHAL – THE UNSTOPPABLE TOUR
District Arena @ Terraform | 4 pm
There are playback singers. And then there is Shreya Ghoshal. From romantic ballads to dance numbers, her voice has been part of the soundtrack of multiple generations. Expect nostalgia, high notes and a crowd that knows the lyrics.
Your vibe:
 Bollywood feels + impossible-to-ignore vocals.
NOV 29 | DARSHAN RAVAL – LOVE LETTERS INDIA TOUR
Bhartiya Mall of Bengaluru | 6 pm
Bring your bestie, your partner or the person you wish was your partner. Darshan Raval’s Love Letters tour promises romantic pop, big sing-alongs and plenty of feelings.
Your vibe:
 soft-launching your relationship status through your Instagram Stories.
NOV 29 | BENNY DAYAL LIVE
Sunburn Union | 7 pm
If sitting through emotional ballads isn't your idea of fun, Benny Dayal has you covered. Expect Bollywood hits, high energy and a dance floor that may be doing considerably more work than you are.
Your vibe: no sitting, only dancing.
NOV 29 | DILJIT DOSANJH – AURA INDIA TOUR
NICE Grounds | 4 pm
And then there’s Diljit. The Punjabi superstar arrives with Aura, bringing together music, pop culture, fashion and the kind of global fanbase that can turn a concert into a full-blown cultural moment. This isn't just a gig. It is an event.
DECEMBER - The grand finale
Thought November was chaotic? December has decided to end the year with a bang — and several bass drops. Electronic music, global pop and one of Bengaluru's biggest music festivals make this a month for serious concert-goers.
DEC 5–6 | ECHOES OF EARTH
Foothills of Nandi Hills
This isn't a “go for two hours and come home” kind of festival. Echoes of Earth combines electronic music, immersive art, elaborate installations and sustainability for a weekend-long experience.
Your vibe:
 festival fits, friends, music, art and approximately 4,000 photos for the ‘gram.
DEC 12–13 | FRED AGAIN..
NICE Grounds | 3 pm
Two days. One of electronic music's biggest current names. Fred again.. has built a reputation for live shows that are as emotional as they are electronic, turning personal stories and samples into massive communal experiences.
Your vibe:
 dance, feel things, dance again.
DEC 15 | KHALID LIVE
Bhartiya Mall of Bengaluru | 6 pm
After the electronic high, things get smoother. Khalid brings his R&B-pop sound to Bengaluru, with the kind of laid-back tracks that have lived on playlists, late-night drives and questionable 2 am decisions.
Your vibe:
 chill, sing along, pretend you're in a music video.
DEC 20 | THE CHAINSMOKERS
NICE Grounds | 4 pm
And just before Christmas, The Chainsmokers take over. Expect dance-pop, massive hooks, big production and enough nostalgia to transport anyone who had Closer on repeat.
Your vibe:
 throwback hits, dance-floor chaos and ending the year loud.

stories.headline: 2.8 lakh SIR hearings still pending in Karnataka, Bengaluru accounts for nearly two-thirds
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Over 2.8 lakh hearings under the special intensive revision (SIR) of Karnataka’s electoral rolls are pending, with the last round due Monday. Bengaluru Urban and three BBMP districts account for 1.8 lakh of them.
According to the chief electoral officer (CEO), 43.8 lakh notices have been generated, and 43.7 lakh delivered (99.8%). Hearings are done in 40.9 lakh cases (93.5%). The 8,570 undelivered notices include 3,522 in Bengaluru. Belgaum has the lowest delivery rate at 96.1%, with 3,252 notices yet to reach voters.
BBMP South has the biggest backlog, with 65,335 hearings pending (84.4% done), followed by Bengaluru Urban with 54,943. Gulbarga is the slowest outside Bengaluru with 80.6% completed, followed by Bidar (85.1%) and Bangalore Rural (86%). Koppal has finished all hearings. Bengaluru accounts for 24.1 lakh notices, about 55% of the state total.
Claims and objections must be disposed of by Oct 22, and the final roll will be published on Oct 27.
Since June 16, as many as 23 lakh forms have been received by Election Commission, led by Form 8 (12.3 lakh) and Form 6 (9.5 lakh). 
Bengaluru Urban alone received 2.6 lakh. Form 7, used to object to the inclusion or deletion of a name, was filed 1.1 lakh times, most often in Shivamogga (6,987), Dakshina Kannada (6,762) and Bidar (6,101).
Amid reports of bulk Form 7 filings that are allegedly not genuine, CEO V Anbukkumar has directed electoral registration officers (EROs) to act against anyone making knowingly false statements in Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8.
Election Commission (ECI) has also ordered a special drive to enrol left-out and first-time voters. Booth-level officers will compare the current roll with the pre-SIR one, list missing names and visit homes, covering 20-25 electors a week over about a month. They will help eligible people fill Form 6 and share the lists with party agents and EROs. Camps will be held at booths, night shelters and labour colonies. Anyone not on the roll can apply at any time.
Since June 16, as many as 23 lakh forms have been received by Election Commission, led by Form 8 (12.3 lakh) and Form 6 (9.5 lakh). Bengaluru Urban alone received 2.6 lakh.
Govt is reportedly considering setting up a special investigation team (SIT) to investigate nine cases registered across the state over alleged attempts to delete voters through bulk Form 7 applications during SIR. CM 
DK Shivakumar
 and DCM G Parameshwara held consultations with senior police officials to determine whether the cases were interconnected. Shivakumar accused BJP of conspiring to manipulate electoral rolls, saying an investigation was needed to establish who directed workers to submit the applications and who supplied them.
HC grants stay on FIRs
The high court Friday granted interim stay on FIRs registered against BJP booth-level agents (BLAs) over filing bulk Form-7 applications for deletion of voters.
Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde passed the order after hearing the petitions filed by Deepak Singh R and GS Vasanthalakshmi.
Yeshwantpur police had registered the FIR against Deepak in relation to Form-7 applications seeking deletion of 136 voters in Malleswaram assembly constituency. It followed a complaint filed by Anoop Iyengar, who contested as a Congress candidate in the 2023 election from that constituency. The FIR against Vasanthalakshmi was registered by Vyalikaval police with regard to 778 Form-7 applications filed by her. It was based on another complaint by Iyengar.
The petitioners have argued that there is no wrongdoing on their part and added that the officials can still verify the veracity of the genuineness of the voters against whom they submitted applications.
Police argued that as against the permissible limit of 50 Form-7s one can file, the petitioners have submitted in excess of the limit with an ulterior motive seeking deletion of a large number of voters.
However, Justice Hegde queried as to whether filing Form-7 applications beyond the limit of 50 is considered an offence under the law.
The judge pointed out that before deleting a name from the voters’ list, the authorities are required to issue a notice to the voter concerned and added that the complaint appears to be hasty and premature in nature.

stories.headline: SIR protest: Former Bengaluru top cop and BJP leader Bhaskar Rao seeks verification of Dhruv Rathee’s citizenship, visa conditions
stories.bodyText:
Former Bengaluru Police Commissioner and BJP leader Bhaskar Rao has written to the Union Home Secretary seeking verification of YouTuber Dhruv Rathee’s citizenship, immigration status, and compliance with visa conditions following his participation in a protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bengaluru’s Freedom Park on Thursday.
In his letter dated October 8, Mr. Rao, who contested the Chamarajpet Assembly constituency representing the BJP in the 2023 polls, said the protest, attended by actor Prakash Raj, the Cockroach Janta Party’s Abhijeet Dipke and others, concerned the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the ongoing SIR exercise.
Mr. Rao said Mr. Rathee was understood to hold German citizenship and sought verification of his nationality, the passport used to enter India, the category of visa or other immigration permission under which he was staying in the country, the purpose and duration of his visit, and the conditions attached. He also sought verification of whether Mr. Rathee held an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card or any other status governing his activities in India.
The former police commissioner requested the Ministry to verify whether Mr. Rathee’s participation in and address at the protest were permissible under the applicable immigration and visa regulations.
He also sought verification of whether Mr. Rathee had participated in similar political activities, demonstrations, and public meetings during earlier visits to India and whether such participation complied with the conditions governing his stay.
Mr. Rao urged the Ministry to take appropriate action in accordance with the law if any violation of the Foreigners Act, 1946, immigration regulations, visa conditions, OCI regulations, or other applicable laws was established. He also requested that relevant immigration and entry and exit records be preserved.
Mr. Rao also stressed that the letter was not motivated by any disagreement with Mr. Rathee’s political opinions or criticism of the government or the Election Commission, but was intended to ensure compliance with the legal framework governing foreign nationals in India.

briefs.headline: TOI report on flyover death in Bengaluru prompts govt action
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A day after 
TOI reported that a Bengaluru-based businessman from Kerala died following a heart attack while he remained stuck in traffic for nearly an hour though the nearest hospital was just metres away, Karnataka govt has directed Bengaluru City police, public works department and infrastructure development department to take necessary action.
The office of chief secretary Shalini Rajneesh took note of 
TOI
’s Oct 8 report and issued a directive.
The action followed after Haralur Road citizen-activist and ex-serviceman Jasjit Singh Gill wrote a letter to chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
. Citing 
TOI
’s report, Gill described death of KK Sajir as “extraordinarily harrowing”.
Sajir was travelling in a car with a friend when he complained of severe chest pain while stuck on a flyover near Chandapura. He died waiting for the traffic to clear. The nearest hospital was right under the flyover.
Gill said while Bengaluru is rapidly expanding its elevated network, numerous flyovers and expressways become traps during gridlocks, offering zero emergency escape. In his letter, he recommended a five-point formula that includes a proposal to integrate emergency lifts and stretcher stairwells and better inter-agency coordination protocols.
“(Please) direct agencies like NHAI, K-Ride, BBMP, and traffic police to establish clear accountability protocols during ongoing construction work so that temporary bottlenecking does not completely immobilize emergency vehicles,” he wrote.
The appeal was initially forwarded to the city police commissioner, who sent it to the Bengaluru Traffic Police. Asked what specific action would be taken, assistant commissioner of police (traffic planning) Prabhakara G did not offer comments.

briefs.headline: After Karnataka’s letters, central govt announces cap on cancer drugs
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Karnataka’s health department has welcomed the Centre’s move to cap trade margins at 30% of the maximum retail price (MRP) for all non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs.
In a letter to Union health minister 
JP Nadda
 in Sept, health minister UT Khader had sought national-level intervention to curb excessive patient billing for cancer drugs, medical devices and consumables procured by hospitals at discounted institutional rates.
Citing an inspection by the Karnataka health department, Khader had highlighted that the analysis had found that certain medicines and consumables were being sold at mark-ups ranging from around three to over 50 times the procurement cost.
Khader had sought the formation of a central inter-ministerial expert group, a national study of high-value medicines and devices, tighter trade-margin caps, mandatory disclosure of procurement costs and patient billing prices, and expanded price regulation by National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA).
“The Centre’s decision to cap trade margins at 30% of the MRP is a significant policy change following Karnataka’s investigation,” health department officials said.
Earlier in Sept, 
TOI
 had reported that Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner Srinivas K had written to the Centre on two separate occasions — first, flagging the huge gap between the landing cost and MRP of medicines, and second, seeking price regulation for essential medical devices to reduce patients’ out-of-pocket expenditure.

briefs.headline: Smart parking in Bengaluru: Relief for Jayanagar residents
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Jayanagar residents will not have to pay fees for vehicles parked in front of their homes under the new smart parking system, Bengaluru South City Corporation commissioner KN Ramesh said Friday.
The system is expected to be implemented soon in the prime south Bengaluru locality to ease traffic congestion and improve parking availability. However, parking charges will apply on major commercial roads between 9am and 10pm, the commissioner said.
The clarification came after representatives of Jayanagar Traders’ Association raised concerns over the proposed parking policy. The traders sought a reduction in parking fees and free parking for the first 30 minutes. Ramesh said the corporation will examine the practical implications of their demands before taking a decision.
He said smart parking system will be restricted to key commercial roads and won’t cover residential stretches. Under the technology-driven system, select roads in Jayanagar will have CCTV surveillance, mobile-based information on real-time parking availability and variable message signboards.
Representatives of Park Lens, the agency involved in the project, said the system will help motorists locate designated parking spaces while also curbing unauthorised parking.

briefs.headline: Future beyond education: Green card move rattles US-bound students in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The US administration’s move to suspend eight major technology companies from the employment-based green card process is the latest setback for youngsters preparing to follow their US aspirations, experts say.
The US department of labour Thursday said it would neither accept new Permanent Labor Certification applications involving these firms nor process pending ones from Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, 
Infosys
, TCS, 
Wipro
, HCL Technologies and Capgemini. The order might create more uncertainty for H-1B workers nearing the standard limit of six years.
“The announcement may not have immediate impact on Indian students. However, the constant policy announcements and uncertainty over the past year have prompted many Indian families to look at alternatives in Europe, Singapore, Hong Kong and other destinations,” said Abhishek Malani, founder, Quest For Success, a Bengaluru-based education consultancy.
More than students, their families are becoming more selective about which American universities would justify the financial investment.
“We must remember that students entering university today will graduate 4-5 years from now. Immigration policies could look different by then. I wouldn’t advise families to make such an important long-term decision based entirely on today’s political climate,” he added.
Karan Lalit, executive director – South Asia, TOEFL & GRE, ETS, said that while the US continues to be an important destination for higher education, research and innovation, students are evaluating international education options amid evolving US immigration policies; factors such as academic quality, affordability, post-study opportunities and visa pathways are shaping their decisions.
“Germany, for instance, now hosts 60,000 Indian students, marking a 20% year-on-year increase. France, the Netherlands and Ireland, too, are gaining attention alongside established destinations such as the US, UK and Canada, reflecting students’ expanding horizons.”
Aritra Ghosal, founder and CEO, OneStep Global, said the recent US developments are a reminder that students need to plan for their careers beyond the decision of where to study. “While the suspension of PERM processing for applications involving specific technology companies does not directly restrict student visas, it raises questions about the longer-term employment and immigration pathways students consider when choosing the US,” he said.
“One of the biggest risks is building a career plan around a single expected outcome: graduating, finding a job and eventually settling overseas. These pathways depend on factors beyond a student’s control, including employer requirements and immigration policies. Students must therefore consider how transferable their skills are, whether their qualifications hold value across markets, and what alternatives remain open if their plans change. An international education should expand their career options, not leave their future dependent on one country or immigration pathway,” he said.
Ritika Singh, executive director, IC3, said there is also an “inward mobility.” “There are liberal arts private universities that are ranked well. There are foreign universities coming in as well as Indian universities that are starting campuses abroad,” she said.

briefs.headline: Winter migrants set to arrive, but Bengaluru’s Hebbal lake revamp still six months away
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The sight of a largely dry Hebbal Lake continues to greet commuters on Airport Road and the Outer Ring Road, even as the winter migration season approaches and more than 90 acres of the lake is yet to undergo desilting.Bengaluru: The sight of a largely dry Hebbal lake continues to greet commuters on Airport Road and Outer Ring Road, even as the winter migration season approaches and over 90 acres of the lake are yet to undergo desilting.
Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials in charge of the project told TOI the lake’s inlets are open, but recent rain has not resulted in significant water accumulation in the main waterbody. However, the newly developed wetlands have received water inflow. “Though the catchment area received good rain in the last two weeks, the areas downstream received heavier rainfall; 16 acres of wetlands have filled up and they are looking beautiful,” a senior official said.
The lake was dewatered in Jan for desilting and comprehensive redevelopment. The first phase of work, including desilting of over 25 acres and development of wetlands, was completed between Jan and Sept. The second and major phase is yet to begin.
GBA is set to open financial bids for the second phase. “We have finished desilting over 25 acres and developing wetlands. Over 90 acres of the waterbody is yet to be desilted. 
The first phase of the project went on from Jan to Sept, while the next phase might take around six months after awarding of tender,” an official said, adding that the tendering process could take another 2-3 weeks.
The Rs 32-crore project covers desilting, pitching (installing stones on the lake embankments), installation of weirs and wetland development. The prolonged dry condition has also raised concern among birdwatchers, particularly with migratory birds expected to arrive during the winter season.
Elizabeth S, from Hebbal Nature Society, said Hebbal lake has long been a popular bird-watching hotspot in Bengaluru, particularly for migratory birds. “Several of the migratory species that visit are entitled to high statutory protection,” she said.
She said migratory birds travel to Bengaluru from Central Asia, Europe and Africa during winter, with the migration season extending from Oct to March. “We need to see how prolonged drying of the lakebed could have a long-term impact on their habitat,” she added.
The project is being implemented by GBA’s Project Implementation Unit, the nodal agency for lake and stormwater drain improvement projects in Bengaluru, under a World Bank loan.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru baker Smriti Nambiar wins silver at WorldSkills competition in Shanghai
briefs.deck: Smriti Nambiar speaks about her journey from Bengaluru and Delhi, to China
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru-based baker Smriti Nambiar won a silver at the 48th WorldSkills Competition held in Shanghai recently. Conducted between September 22 and 27, it is one of the biggest international competitions for vocational and technical skills. Five other women represented India across five significant hospitality categories.
Along with the silver medal, Smriti has also been recognised as India’s ‘Best of the Nation’ competitor. This places her achievement high on the global stage and strongly represents her skills within and outside India. WorldSkills brought together 68 countries and regions across 64 skills in six distinct sectors. In the bakery category, 22 competitors participated from across the globe.
Smriti grew up in Bengaluru and did her schooling in Sarjapur, graduating in Hotel Management from IHM Pusa, New Delhi. She says, “I was always passionate about pastries and baking, and wanted to work in that field. Even though I didn’t know much about it while applying, through this competition, I learnt a lot about baking and was able to carry my skills forward.”
Talking about the competition, she says, “The event was organised on a massive scale. Everything from crowd management to time efficiency was perfect. For the bakery section, we were provided with everything from equipment to ingredients.”
Her mentor Avin Thaliath, co-founder of the Lavonne Academy, played a vital role in her training. He says, “Smriti’s silver at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 is a landmark achievement for her and a proud moment for Indian baking. As her mentor and coach, my role was to help her develop the technical discipline, precision and confidence needed to compete at the highest level, but it was her perseverance, composure and relentless pursuit of excellence that ultimately brought her to the podium.”
Smriti trained for two years, but says the most rigorous period was the last four months before the competition. “They give us a module list of breads, and we had to practice how to prepare them. We had to create 16 modules across two days which included pain au chocolat croissant, cinnamon rolls, cream buns, baguette and two types of sourdough.”

briefs.headline: Read A Kitaab debuts their literature festival in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: After two successful editions in Mumbai, Read A Kitaab is hosting their literature festival in Bengaluru for the first time
briefs.bodyText:
Read A Kitaab is hosting a two-day literature festival in Bengaluru on October 10 and 11 at Atta Galatta in Indiranagar. They have hosted two editions in Mumbai, where the book-club began four years ago; this will be the festival’s debut in Bengaluru.
Founded by Ekta Bhandari and Anurag Kothari, Read A Kitaab initially started as a book community that hosted meetings in Mumbai and online. Today, they have chapters across 12 cities in India with over thirty thousand members. Their book-club hosts thematic monthly book-meets and online Book of the Month discussions.
“It is a community that was built with the aim of bringing back a love for reading and the written word. The idea was to nudge people to read more and broaden their perspectives,” says Ekta.
After Mumbai, their second chapter was launched in Bengaluru. Talking about their Bengaluru readers, Ekta says it has been three years since the book club began here, and adds, “the participants have always been eclectic and provided diverse insights into discussions.”
Anurag says, “The way literature has been nurtured in Bengaluru is quite different. We have seen readers from different age groups, from little child and adults to senior citizens participate.” He highlights Atta Galatta’s continued assistance, “From hosting our monthly meets to our first ever literature festival in Bengaluru, we have always received tremendous support from them.”
The founders want this initiative to be a travelling literature festival that goes from city to city, with a focus on authors and poets from those regions. Their reason for choosing Bengaluru is clear — the number of authors based in the city as well as their active book-club members.
The festival is hosting prominent authors including Vivek Shanbagh, Milan Vohra, Mani Rao, Shinie Anthony and others. Academic and philosopher Sundar Sarukkai, sports journalists Sandeep Menon and Sharda Ugra who will hold discussions during the festival.
“We want to create new readers with this festival,” says Ekta, adding, “Bring a friend who has never read a book and get them to attend these interesting panels. They might change their minds.” The panel discussions will revolve around topics such as romance, poetry, music, cinema, mental health and more.
“The speciality of this festival is that all the panellists moderating the sessions are readers with the club, and not professional moderators.”

stories.headline: States to assess GDP through spending method
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: For decades, a state's growth was measured by relying only on the production approach, or by gauging what factories, farms, and services within its borders produced. That model is now set for an overhaul, as the statistics ministry unveiled a new manual to compute state GDP via expenditure approach -- by tracking household spending, govt outlays, capital investments, and net trade.
This marks the attempt to track how consumer habits have evolved over time, including explicitly logging modern household costs-ranging from OTT streaming subscriptions and DTH fees to specialised personal care items like face washes, hair serums, and electric grooming tools.

stories.headline: US trade talks steady, visa curbs may help India: Piyush Goyal
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Commerce and industry minister 
Piyush Goyal
 said on Friday that talks with US for a trade deal were progressing steadily and the two sides were working on the fine print, while asserting that tighter access to H-1B visas can benefit India by encouraging skilled professionals to stay back, bringing more tech work to the country and boosting the startup ecosystem.
The minister's comments come days after USTR Jaimeson Greer said that a deal was not imminent, and FM Nirmala Sitharaman stated that talks had hit a plateau. "Going by what the US itself has said, it has nothing more to add or offer, and the fine print is being worked out," Goyal said at the ET Startup Awards 2026 held in Bengaluru on Friday.
"The key issue is how the US will give us the comparative advantage we had agreed upon in Feb. That requires legal expertise, which AI cannot provide, because this goes beyond the textbook. That is what we are working on," he said.
The trade minister, who just returned from US, said several American companies had outlined their plans for India as they looked to tap the Indian talent pool and highlighted the cost advantage here. "Look at the entire ecosystem and you will realise that every H-1B visa not granted is a big win for India," Goyal said.
Tighter H-1B access could give Indian startups, particularly in deep technology, greater momentum, he said, adding that the sector had significant room to grow in India. Goyal said he had never raised the issue of H-1B visas or green cards in his conversations with US as immigration was not directly related to trade, although the movement of people to deliver services was important.
He said a growing share of technology work was coming to Indian cities as companies recognised the value of setting up GCCs here.

stories.headline: Elon Musk ups ante in Starlink row, sarcastically calls Ambani ‘Prime Minister’, alleges monopoly
stories.deck: The post bybrea Mr. Musk now marks a sharp escalation in the Starlink satcom offering row, which saw the U.S. trillionaire recently alleging that powerful business interests are seeking to block his service
stories.bodyText:
Elon Musk on Friday (October 9, 2026) escalated his public spat over Starlink's entry into India, sarcastically addressing industrialist Mukesh Ambani as “Prime Minister Ambani” and accusing him of seeking to protect a monopoly, while asking if he would consider allowing the satellite internet service to compete in the country.
Mr. Musk's latest salvo on X came just hours after Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia asserted that India does not permit monopolies in any sector, and that despite the buzz around one “particular” company, three players have received satcom licences and can start operations after individually meeting the security requirements and milestones.
The post by Mr. Musk now marks a sharp escalation in the Starlink satcom offering row, which saw the U.S. trillionaire recently alleging that powerful business interests are seeking to block his service to preserve their dominance in the Indian market.
In a post on Thursday (October 8, 2026), Mr. Musk had asked if “Ambani is the real boss of India”.
On Friday (October 9, 2026) evening, Mr. Musk upped the ante with a fresh post.
“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” he wrote.
Mr. Musk also said that there are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market.
“Starlink would change their lives for the better,” Mr. Musk said.
Within minutes, Mr. Musk penned another post, saying, “Starlink has proven to be essential for saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communication systems have failed,” adding, “So you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India.”
On Friday (October 9, 2026), Mr. Scindia said India doesn't allow monopoly in any sector.
“Let me set the record straight. For us, the Department of Telecommunications, we are technology agnostic... Our job is to be able to provide the bouquet of services to every single customer. It is for the customer to choose in a free market which service he or she prefers, and within that service bouquet, which company's service he or she prefers,” the Union minister said at a briefing at the India Mobile Congress in New Delhi.
Mr. Scindia said that three entities – Mr. Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb – have already secured licences, while Amazon's Kuiper has expressed interest and will need to undergo the established procedure.
While there is a lot of conversation about one particular company, three have got satcom licences, he said.
"We are very clear on our stand. There are three parties that have got a licence; as and when the government decides the charge system on the revenue basis, that spectrum will be assigned to them, and as and when they individually fulfil the security conditions, they can start operations,” the Minister said.
TRAI and the telecom department are close to a final decision on pricing regime for satcom spectrum, Mr. Scindia said.
Hitting out at the Congress in the backdrop of Rahul Gandhi and Mr. Musk's exchange on X, the minister said, “As far as the Congress is concerned... I don't think they themselves know whether they're going left or right.”
He said the Congress initially had a problem with "a certain person getting a licence" and pointed out that "now they have a problem, and they've allied with that person in terms of why he's not getting a licence".
“So I don't know whether they have clarity on where they're going, but that is the case with the Congress, which is to be expected," Mr. Scindia said.
The war of words came amid a spat over satcom services, with Mr. Musk alleging that Starlink is being blocked by certain oligarchs seeking to "maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people".
As the India Mobile Congress (IMC) unfolded in the capital, the government and Mr. Musk traded barbs over satellite communications, with the Department of Telecommunications rejecting allegations that domestic business interests were blocking Starlink's entry, prompting the tech billionaire to sarcastically ask whether "Ambani is the real boss of India".
"Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?" Mr. Musk said in an X post earlier.
The Telecom Ministry has maintained that the country's authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is "fair and non-discriminatory" and that any suggestion that it was being applied selectively was "baseless and misconceived".
